walkthrough: Goal: ink in colour, take back part of a line with the eraser, recolour a line without going over its edges, reuse a colour already on the canvas, and find colours, eraser and lock as they were after closing the app.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library. At the top bar's right end, right to left: the colour button (a round swatch of the current colour, black at first), Layers, Eraser (a slanted block) and Brush (highlighted: the pen paints). The side bar holds the size slider, the eyedropper (a pipette) between the sliders, the opacity slider, then undo and redo.

Tap the colour button: the colour panel drops down under it, over the canvas (opening it closes the brush or layer panel). Header Colour; a hue ring around a square of saturation (left to right) and value (bottom to top); below, 'Colours you choose appear here.'

Tap the ring at blue, then drag a finger in the square up to its top-right corner: the marker follows the finger, the swatch in the top bar turns blue at once; lifting the finger puts blue first in the recent colours row. Draw with the pen on the canvas outside the panel: the panel closes and a blue line appears.
Open the colour panel again and tap the ring at red: the colour is red, red joins the front of the recent row. Draw a red line across the blue one.

Tap the Eraser button: it is highlighted, Brush no longer. Tap it again: the brush panel opens headed Eraser, the eraser's own brush highlighted (Ink Pen); tap Soft Brush. Erase down through both lines with the pen: the lines fade under a soft edge towards the white paper (since S16 the soft brush builds up, so going over the place again takes more away). The side bar's sliders now set the eraser's size and opacity; the brush keeps its own.
Tap undo: the lines are whole again; tap redo: erased again. Colour and tool changes are no history steps; strokes and layer changes are.

Tap Layers: under the opacity slider the active layer's Alpha Lock switch; tap it: it turns on and the row reads Alpha Lock. Tap Brush (the pen paints again, the panel stays), open the colour panel and tap blue in the recent row, then draw blue along part of the red line and off it onto the empty paper: the red under the stroke turns blue, its edges as soft as they were, and the paper stays white. The eraser on an alpha-locked layer takes nothing away (as in Procreate); the pen's stroke there leaves no trace and no history step.
Tap undo: the blue stroke is gone; tap undo again: Alpha Lock is off (open Layers: the switch and the row show it).

Tap the eyedropper in the side bar: it is highlighted. Tap the red line with a finger: the colour button turns exactly the red under the finger (read back from the canvas as it shows), red moves to the front of the recent row, the eyedropper turns off and the pen paints again: draw a short line, it is that red. Tapping the eyedropper again before touching the canvas turns it off without picking.

Leave the app and let the system close it, open it again: every stroke looks exactly as before, the layer's Alpha Lock is off as it was left, the colour button is red, the recent colours are in the same order, Brush is the tool and the eraser still uses the Soft Brush.

Failure: a stored toolbox that cannot be read starts at black, the brush tool and no recent colours; it never keeps the drawing from opening. Not here: a loupe under the finger while picking, touch-and-hold or pen-button eyedropper (gesture mapping is the author's), the pen's eraser end, colour harmony or value sliders, palettes.
